instrument_validation: The retraced path gives |A| = 0.00000e+00 exactly, as it must, since reversing an out-and-back path returns the same sequence. The decomposition and measurement carry no numerical junk.
measurement: Signed holonomy H_gamma = F_after(gamma) - F_stay in audit-logit space, decomposed into a common drift S = (H_cw + H_ccw)/2 and an orientation-odd part A = (H_cw - H_ccw)/2. The geometric claim lives entirely in A. Fully deterministic: fixed dataset, full-batch gradient descent, labels rotating with the teacher, identical initialization and step counts, so ORDER is the only difference between paired paths.
new_object_if_revived: Any continuation is a DIFFERENT scientific object and needs a new discovery ID: decaying order-memory with a saturation scale, not geometric phase. The measurable would be the decay length of curriculum memory, not an area law.
not_pursued: No connection, curvature tensor, or Stokes-type relation was defined. Doing so would have been decoration: the ordering test, the scaling exponent, and both zero-area nulls all fail, so there is no measured phenomenon for such a formalism to explain.
title: Curriculum holonomy under the full discriminator suite
verdict: KILLED on every discriminator. Learning has order-dependent path memory, but it is NOT geometric.
what_the_failure_teaches: Orientation-odd path memory is real and not small: |A| is 17 to 58 percent of the common drift. So learning does retain a signed memory of the order in which a curriculum was traversed. But that memory is SUBLINEAR in loop size and its relative weight DECREASES as loops grow, which is the signature of a saturating, decaying memory rather than an accumulating geometric one. The learner forgets early curriculum, so order matters proportionally less over larger excursions. Curvature accumulates; this decays. They are opposite objects.
